newsitem.title: USA: More U.S brokers seen targets of banks.
newsitem.headline: More U.S brokers seen targets of banks.

text.p: The stocks of regional investment banks rose sharply Monday as Wall Street bet that more acquisitions will follow that of Alex. Brown Inc. by Bankers Trust New York Corp.

The $1.7 billion acquisition of Alex. Brown, announced Sunday, comes eight weeks after the $10.2 billion acquisition of Dean Witter Discover & Co. by Morgan Stanley Group Inc., and industry analysts said it portends more to come as the Depression-era law separating the two industries breaks down.

The union of investment banks and commercial banks has long been anticipated amid the gradual erosion of the 1933 Glass-Steagall law. The law remains in effect, but the Federal Reserve recently raised the limit on how much underwriting a bank can do through its securities affiliate.
Frank Newman, chairman of Bankers Trust, said the revision of the regulations was a key factor in his company's buying Baltimore-based Alex. Brown.
He said the combined companies' underwriting revenues will be about 20 percent of securities revenue, which exceeds the old limit of 10 percent but falls within the new limit of 25 percent.
The rationale for the Glass-Steagal Act was that if banks were to offer deposit insurance, they should stay out of "risky" areas like securities.
Newman said corporate clients need a mixture of financial services and that combining Bankers Trust's specialities with those of Alex. Brown would make things easier for the client.
Newman said the deal combined Bankers Trust's expertise in syndicated bank debt and debt securities with Alex. Brown's equities research, distribution and underwriting.
While each company could have built up the speciality where it was not dominant, "building is very long and hard," Newman added.
Bankers Trust paid a substantial premium for Alex. Brown.
Based on Monday's closing prices, Bankers Trust will pay $66.30 a share for Alex Brown, well above the $41.375 it traded for as recently as Wednesday.
Alex. Brown closed Monday at $62.75, up $9.625. Bankers Trust closed at $79.875, down $2.375.
Analysts were concerned that Alex. Brown's earnings might have peaked in 1996.

"That's one reason why Bankers Trust's stock is down today," said George Salem, a banking analyst with Gerard Klauer Mattison. "People might be feareful that Alex. Brown's earnings were at their peak in 1996."
Both Chase Manhattan Corp. and Citicorp have said they are interested in acquiring investment management companies. Chase and Citicorp are the two largest U.S. banks, based on assets.
As for the most likely acquisition candidates, Perrin Long, an independent analyst, said it all depends on a particular bank's strategy.

He said A.G. Edwards Inc., which is based in St. Louis and provides brokerage services to individuals, and Edward D. Jones & Co., also based in St. Louis, would be logical partners for banks interested in the retail side of the business. A.G. Edwards stock was up $1.75 at $35.25 on the New York Stock Exchange. Edward D. Jones is privately held.

"If a bank wants to be in trading it might look at Salomon Brothers," Long added, and if it wants exposure to capital markets, plus a major clearing operation, Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp. would be a candidate. Lehman Brothers would offer capital markets and trading, he said.
Regarding the Alex. Brown and Bankers New York Corp. deal, Long said the two were "a good fit."
"I think Alex. Brown will make a great contribution to Bankers Trust over the years. I can't argue that some people think the price is a little high, but it looks reasonable to me."
Analysts said regional brokerage firms would be candidates for acquisition by the big regional banking powerhouses that have resulted from a wave of banking mergers since the 1980s.

Among regional brokerages, shares of Legg Mason Inc., with brokerage operations in Baltimore and New Orleans, jumped $4 to $49; Morgan Keegan Inc., a brokerage based in Memphis, gained $2.125 to $19; and Minneapolis-based Piper Jaffray Cos. was up $2 at $16.75, all on the New York Stock Exchange.
